from: A regional council is told that Otjiwa Welding employs 90 people with capital employed of N$6 000 000, while Namib Quarry Plant employs 18 people with capital employed of N$42 000 000. Interpret those figures for a council deciding which business does more to support employment in the district, and for a supplier deciding which is the safer business to give credit to.
to: A regional council is told that Otjiwa Welding employs 90 people with capital employed of N$6 000 000, while Namib Quarry Plant employs 18 people with capital employed of N$42 000 000. Explain what those figures mean for a council deciding which business does more to support employment in the district, and for a supplier deciding which is the safer business to give credit to.
why: Interpret is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain. The answer reads the figures against each other and says what they mean, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Namib Leather tans hides and makes bags. It buys hides from one abattoir, which supplies three tanneries and has raised its price twice in a year, and it sells through 40 independent shops, four of which take half its output. It can buy either a share of the abattoir or the four shops. Analyse the circumstances in which each purchase would suit it, and recommend which it should pursue.
to: Namib Leather tans hides and makes bags. It buys hides from one abattoir, which supplies three tanneries and has raised its price twice in a year, and it sells through 40 independent shops, four of which take half its output. It can buy either a share of the abattoir or the four shops. Analyse the circumstances in which each purchase would suit it, and evaluate which it should pursue.
why: Recommend is not used on the current AS papers; the judgement is now asked for with Evaluate. The card keeps its Analyse part, so it pairs the two parts of a Paper 1 Section B question (8 + 12) and no single paper tariff is claimed.
